 “My Bond With Cricket Will Never Break”: Sabbineni Meghana Calls Time on Her Playing Career
 Sabbineni Meghana represented India in 17 WT20Is and three WODIs. By WebDesk October 23, 2026 No Comments 2 Mins Read

 Andhra Pradesh batter Sabbineni Meghana has announced her retirement from all formats of cricket, sharing the news on her social media platforms on Friday.
 The 30-year-old made her international debut on November 20, 2016, in a WT20I against the West Indies. She went on to represent India in 17 WT20Is and three WODIs before bringing her playing career to an end.
 Sharing the news, Meghana posted a heartfelt retirement message, beginning with “Thank You BCCI”. Alongside a picture of herself batting in India’s blue jersey, she mentioned “135-53”, her ODI and T20I cap numbers, respectively.
 Reflecting on her journey, she wrote: “Stepping onto the field for the very first time with a bat in hand to wearing a jersey on the world stage has been nothing short of a dream come true. As I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket as a player, my heart is overflowing with gratitude. The field has been my second home, teaching me resilience, humility, and giving me memories and friendships that I will carry for a lifetime.”
 Meghana also thanked her family, coaches, teammates, support staff and fans for their support throughout her career. She expressed her gratitude to the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), the Andhra Cricket Association (ACA), her two Women’s Premier League (WPL) franchises, Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and Gujarat Giants (GG), as well as RPSB.
 Meghana featured for GG in one WPL season and represented RCB in the other two. Across 14 innings, she scored 302 runs, including one half-century. She was part of the RCB squad that won the title in 2024.
 Concluding her message, Meghana made it clear that her association with the sport would continue beyond her playing days.
 “While my playing days come to an end, my bond with cricket will never break,” she said. “I will always stay deeply connected to the game and intend to dedicate my life to giving back to the sport, mentoring the next generation, and serving the game that gave me everything. Thank you, Cricket. You will forever be my heart, my passion, and my lifelong purpose.”
